title: Noah Schnapp Reveals He Auditioned for Haymitch in Sunrise on the Reaping
excerpt:
The Stranger Things actor tried out for the young Haymitch role.
He publicly praised Joseph Zada as the right choice for the part.
body_md:
Noah Schnapp has revealed that he auditioned to play a young Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. The role ultimately went to Joseph Zada, and Schnapp has responded to that decision with a supportive public message rather than disappointment or criticism.

On Saturday, the Stranger Things actor shared an Instagram Story referencing his audition. He tagged Zada and said that the filmmakers had made the right choice. The post offered a rare glimpse into a casting process for a major franchise role without suggesting any conflict between the performers.

Sunrise on the Reaping centers on Haymitch’s experience in the 50th Hunger Games and the early events that shape his place in Panem’s history. Adapted from Suzanne Collins’s 2025 novel, the film explores a younger version of a character audiences already know from the original films. Zada leads a cast that also includes McKenna Grace, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Maya Hawke.

The movie follows the franchise’s earlier prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, and continues its exploration of Panem before Katniss Everdeen’s story. By shifting the perspective to Haymitch, it offers a new context for a familiar character whose later experiences were central to the original series.

The casting revelation arrives alongside a strong theatrical opening. According to the report, Sunrise on the Reaping earned $120 million domestically and $105 million internationally during its opening weekend, for a worldwide debut of $225 million. Those figures describe the initial release period, not the film’s eventual lifetime gross.

Schnapp, meanwhile, is pursuing other work. He is appearing in Andy Sandberg’s play Affluenza at Riverside Studios in London, marking his professional stage debut. The dark comedy, inspired by real events, follows Dylan, a 16-year-old confronting the aftermath of causing a fatal drunk-driving accident in the Hamptons.

The stage cast also includes Janette Manrara, Juliet Cowan, Wallis Currie-Wood and Rupert Young. Schnapp’s revelation therefore highlights both the competition surrounding a coveted franchise role and the different opportunities available to an actor whose audition did not result in a casting announcement. His public response keeps the emphasis on respect for the colleague who secured the part.
